changes.before: if chooses instructions using true or false.
changes.after: Use if and else to choose which instructions run.

before: Before this: Kotlin lesson 3, Add numbers. You will reuse the earlier display function and value names.
A Boolean is a value that is either true or false. The comparison >= means greater than or equal to.
An if checks its condition. A condition is the true-or-false expression inside the parentheses.
When pages is 3, pages >= 3 is true, so the first block runs. Otherwise else supplies the other block; both do not run.

Expected output from this example, explained rather than executed here:
```text
Goal met
```
after: A condition is a question with a `true` or `false` answer. Kotlin calls this kind of answer a Boolean.
The symbol `>=` means greater than or equal to. Here, `pages >= 3` asks whether the page count is at least 3.
The word `if` checks the condition in parentheses. When it is true, Kotlin runs the instructions inside the first pair of curly braces.
The word `else` gives the instructions for a false answer. Only one of these two paths runs.
The screen shows `Goal met`. The value of `pages` is 3, so it passes the at-least-3 check.
